body.question: You rub a balloon on your hair and it sticks to a wall. Why?
options: Rubbing makes it sticky like glue
Rubbing charges it, and the charged balloon is attracted to particles in the wall
Rubbing fills it with warm air that rises
body.reveal: When two materials touch or rub, electrons or ions can move from one to the other, leaving one with positive charge and the other with an equal negative charge. A balloon rubbed on hair becomes negatively charged. Near a wall it is attracted to positively charged particles there, and can cling against gravity.
